Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The fed funds rate is 5.33 with no change over 12 months, so the Fed is on hold at the peak. The unemployment rate is 4.1%, up 0.5pp over 12 months. Core CPI is 3.28% and headline is 2.98%, which fits mid-2024. The 10-year yield at 4.15% fell 0.54pp over 3 months, which points to a September 2024 peak in rate-cut expectations, but the policy rate is still 5.33 at that point, so the Fed has not yet cut. The Fed cut in September 2024 (to 4.83), so the snapshot must predate that.

Unemployment at 4.1% and payrolls averaging 177k fit June 2024 (4.1%) or July 2024 (4.3%). Core CPI YoY was 3.27% in June 2024 and headline 2.97%, which matches. The 10-year yield ended June 2024 near 4.36%, but the snapshot says 4.15%. The 2-year at 4.35% is close to the June 2024 close of 4.75%, though not exact. That is a poor match, so I considered the alternatives.

Core CPI in June 2024 was 3.3% and headline 3.0%, a good fit. Yet the 3m change in the 10-year is -0.54, and the 10-year at the end of March 2024 was 4.20%, so a drop by June would not work. Using July 2024 data instead, the 10-year closed near 4.03% and the 2-year near 4.26%. Core CPI for July was 3.2% and headline 2.9%. The 3m change in core of -0.52 fits better with June or July. The 10-year at 4.15% and the 2-year at 4.35% sit between those months, so the snapshot is probably from July 2024.

US equity gained 1.0% in the month with 10.1% over 3 months, and gold gained 5.1% in the month. Gold rose in July 2024 and fell back in the 12m drawdown. Treasuries 7-10y gained 3.7% in the month, which fits July 2024 (yields fell sharply in late July and early August). Unemployment of 4.1% in the snapshot suggests June data, but the July report of 4.3% came out on Aug 2. Month-end July 2024 therefore fits the market data, with the macro data still showing the June unemployment rate.
